build.summary: I made all three follow-ups. The over-rotation card now starts in 'coaxial-rca' instead of 'near-rca'. Its preset ('torque') and catheter (JR4) are unchanged, and so is the teaching moment: the JR4 sits close to the RCA ostium, lined up but not seated, and the learner must seat it with fine torque without swinging past. With the fixed thresholds, a JR4 reached 'near-rca' in only 9 of 40 freshly generated torque cases and in none of the library RCA cases. It reached 'coaxial-rca' in 40 of 40. The engagement thresholds were not loosened. The Settings difficulty text now says that difficulty changes the help given (hints and attending prompts) and that engagement uses the same tolerance at every difficulty. The physics registry tests no longer assume src/ui/physics/impl/ is empty. All four acceptance test files pass and the typecheck is clean. One gap remains: in the current code, difficulty does not change hints or attending prompts (see notes).

outOfScope: The difficulty setting does not yet change hints or attending prompts anywhere in the code. Hints and the attending drawer follow the level policy (policyFor in src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts and src/ui/lab/visibility.ts), not profile.difficulty. The new Settings text states the behaviour the plan intends (diag-engagement-fallback: 'difficulty changes assistance (hints and attending prompts) only'). Making it true needs a change in useSimulatorStore.ts and/or src/ui/lab/visibility.ts or src/mentor/visibility.ts, which this package does not own.

review.verdict: Accept. The package does what its brief asks. All three follow-ups are in place, and the four acceptance test files plus the new Settings.test.ts pass (82 + 66 tests). npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit exits 0. The only changed files are the four listed ones and one new test file, src/ui/sections/Settings.test.ts. The other files under src/ that are newer than .started (content.test.ts, lab/tips.ts, lab/tips.test.ts, lab/raisable/waiting.ts, simulation/access/route.ts) are all in the snapshot sets of repair-launch-fixture-and-tip-ties or access-multi-site, which started at the same time. engagement.ts and analysis.ts are untouched, the thresholds were not loosened, and shared engine defaults are unchanged. src/ui/physics/impl/ still does not exist. The over-rotation card now starts at 'coaxial-rca' with preset 'torque' and catheter JR4. This class sits inside the fixed near-ostium distance, aligned but not seated. The over-rotation check in analysis.ts runs for any '-rca' class, so the teaching moment survives. The physics registry tests no longer depend on impl/ being empty. They glob __fixtures__/impl on its own, and the real-folder test checks against collectPhysicsDevices(REAL)[0], which uses the same sort as getPhysicsDevices. The Settings markup follows the design system (stat-label, text-[12px] text-ink-faint) and is in British English. No clinical numbers were added, no ground truth appears on live screens, and nothing new runs per frame. One real problem remains, confirmed independently and outside this package's files: the new Settings text says difficulty changes hints and attending prompts, and no code does that yet.

findings.problem: The Settings page now says difficulty changes the help given ('The most help: hints and attending prompts...', 'Less help', 'The least help'), but no code does this. A grep across src shows profile.difficulty reaches only FreeLab.tsx, which passes it to loadCase, and Challenge.tsx, which forces 'advanced'. Inside the simulator store, mentor host and start search it goes only to computeEngagement and findStartControls, and both ignore it unless difficultyScaled is set. Hints and the attending drawer follow policyFor, the level policy, not difficulty. After this package, the setting changes nothing a learner can see, and the page tells them it does. The text matches the brief and the plan's intent, so this is not the builder's fault, but the UI now makes a false claim.
findings.fix: Raise a follow-up repair package that owns src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts and src/ui/lab/visibility.ts (or src/mentor/visibility.ts). In it, make difficulty set the hint and attending-prompt policy, for example beginner = policy defaults, intermediate = no proactive hints, advanced = no hints or attending prompts except safety-critical ones. Add a test that each of the three difficulties produces a different hint and attending visibility. If that package cannot land soon, change the three DIFF_HINT strings to describe current behaviour only, for example keep 'the daily challenge and exam mode always use it' and drop the 'most/less/least help' claims, so the page stays true in the meantime.

findings.problem: The new brief reads 'The JR4 sits just short of the RCA ostium. Fine torque only: seat it without swinging past.' From 'coaxial-rca', computeEngagement often tells the learner to change height ('The tip is a touch high; come down gently.' or 'a touch low; withdraw slightly'), so seating may need insertion rather than torque. 'Fine torque only' can then contradict the live engagement message. The error being drilled is still over-rotation, so this is wording only.
findings.fix: Reword the brief to keep the torque caution without forbidding insertion, for example: 'The JR4 sits just short of the RCA ostium, lined up. Seat it with small movements and do not torque past the ostium.'

fix.notes:
I checked all four findings against the code and applied all four.

1 (major, Settings text). Confirmed. profile.difficulty only reaches loadCase (FreeLab.tsx) and the forced 'advanced' in Challenge.tsx. Inside the engine it only goes to computeEngagement and findStartControls, and both ignore it unless difficultyScaled is set. Hints and the attending drawer follow resolveLabPolicy in src/ui/lab/visibility.ts, which uses the entrustment level, the launched activity or exam mode. Difficulty plays no part in it. I applied the reviewer's interim option so the page now describes what the code does. DIFFICULTY_NOTE now reads: "Catheter engagement is judged against the same tolerance at every difficulty. Hints and attending prompts follow your entrustment level and the activity you open, not this setting." The DIFF_HINT lines are now "The default for new profiles." (beginner), "Engagement is judged as at every other difficulty." (intermediate) and "The daily challenge and exam mode always use it." (advanced). This departs from the brief's wording, which asked the page to say difficulty changes the help given, because that claim is false in the current code. The code comment in Settings.tsx explains why.

outOfScope follow-up: a repair package that owns src/state/useSimulatorStore.ts and src/ui/lab/visibility.ts (or src/mentor/visibility.ts) should make difficulty set the hint and attending-prompt policy. It should add a test that the three difficulties produce different visibility, then restore the 'changes the help given' wording in Settings.tsx and Settings.test.ts.

2 (minor, over-rotation brief). Applied. The brief now reads: "The JR4 sits just short of the RCA ostium, lined up. Seat it with small movements and do not torque past the ostium."

3 (minor, dissection and air-embolism start states). Confirmed with a probe: on fresh seeds, dissection resolved 11 of 15 and air-embolism 13 of 15. I fixed it in skillCards.ts, which is a listed file, by pinning library cases that resolve, fit each card's preset and are not exam held-out cases (I checked this with classifyCase). Dissection now uses caseId 'left-main-lesion-0' (preset left-main, near-lm, resolves with JL4.5). Air-embolism now uses 'rca-damping-0' (preset damping, selective-rca, resolves with JR4). Review.launchCard already prefers caseId, so no other file changes. I added a test to mentor.test.ts: 'every diagnostic card with a start class resolves on the case Review launches it on, for any seed'. A pinned card must resolve on its case; an unpinned card must resolve on 12 generated seeds. All cards pass.

4 (minor, test name). Applied. The Settings.test.ts test is renamed 'engagement is judged the same at every difficulty', and the describe and first test now match the new text. The first test also asserts that no 'most/less/least help' or 'difficulty changes the help' claim appears.

I created a temporary probe folder, src/__probe_tmp, and deleted it afterwards.

problems.where: src/mentor/skillCards.ts, 'over-rotation' template (line 104), launched from src/ui/sections/Review.tsx launchCard
problems.problem: The card always resolves to JR4 'coaxial-rca', but Review generates a fresh 'torque' case for every launch. In 10 of 40 such cases the JR4 cannot reach 'selective-rca' anywhere on the insertion -12..30 by torque -3..3 grid. The brief tells the learner to 'Seat it with small movements', and the pass rule is failedAttempts.right <= 1. On about a quarter of launches the task cannot be done, and failed approaches pile up, so the card fails and is rescheduled for a reason the learner cannot fix.
problems.fix: In skillCards.ts only, pin the card to a library case that a JR4 both approaches coaxially and can seat: add caseId: 'easy-rca-0' to the start. Review uses caseId ahead of the preset, and easy-rca-0 gives coaxial [ins 0, tq 0] and seated [ins -0.5, tq 0.1]. Keep preset 'torque' and catheterId 'JR4'. Then add a mentor.test.ts assertion that findStartControls(case, 'JR4', 'selective-rca') is non-null for this card's case. The alternative is to keep generated cases and have resolveDiagnosticStart reject cases where the card's catheter cannot seat, but that needs a change to Review.tsx (out of scope) or an extra filter inside skillCards.ts.

problems.problem: The package acceptance asks the text to say that difficulty changes the help given (hints, attending prompts). The rendered text says the opposite: help follows entrustment level and the activity, not this setting. This is true to the current code, where difficulty no longer changes engagement, hints or prompts, but it does not meet the acceptance as worded. The setting now has no visible effect, and the intermediate line 'Engagement is judged as at every other difficulty.' tells the learner nothing.
problems.fix: The plan owner decides. Either accept the truthful wording and record the acceptance change, or wire difficulty into resolveLabPolicy (src/ui/lab/visibility.ts, outside this package) and then restore the wording the acceptance asks for. If the truthful wording stays, change the intermediate line to something informative, for example 'Kept for older profiles; it does not change engagement or help.', or remove the selector until difficulty does something.

problems.problem: The resolver picks the smallest hub excursion, which can sit at the edge of the coaxial window. On seed card:verify:2 a +0.05 torque nudge already leaves 'coaxial-rca' for 'non-selective'. On those seeds the card starts one jitter away from losing the start class.
problems.fix: For this card, prefer the middle of the target class: among grid points in the target class with the same insertion, pick the torque at the centre of the contiguous torque run, or add a margin penalty such as rejecting points whose ±0.05 torque neighbours are outside the class.
